notes: Flat 4.4% rate for tax year 2026 (DOR 2026 DR 0104EP worksheet). The TABOR-triggered temporary rate reduction does not apply to 2026.
Colorado starts from federal taxable income, so the federal standard (or itemized) deduction is already applied; Colorado standard deduction and personal exemption are therefore 0 here.

For tax years 2026 and later, taxpayers with federal AGI over $300,000 must add back federal standard or itemized deductions in excess of $1,000 (single) / $2,000 (joint). This addback is not modeled, so tax is understated above $300,000 AGI.
Taxpayers with AGI over $500,000 (single) or $1,000,000 (joint) must add back the federal QBI deduction (made permanent from 2026 by HB25B-1001); not modeled.
Colorado subtractions (e.g., state income tax refunds, pension/Social Security subtraction), credits (e.g., Colorado EITC and child tax credit) and Colorado AMT are not modeled.

seDeduction.note: Inherited: federal taxable income already reflects the deductible half of SE tax.

retirementContributions.note: SEP-IRA and solo 401(k) deductions are inherited through federal taxable income.

qbi.note: Federal taxable income is after the QBI deduction, so Colorado keeps it, except single filers with AGI over $500,000 and joint filers over $1,000,000 must add it back.

localIncomeTax.note: No Colorado locality taxes income. Several cities (e.g., Denver) levy flat monthly occupational privilege (head) taxes on workers and businesses, which are not income-based and are not modeled.

estimatedTax.threshold: Required if you expect to owe more than $1,000 of Colorado net tax for 2026 after withholding and credits.
estimatedTax.safeHarbor: Required annual payment is the smaller of 70% of 2026 net Colorado tax or 100% of 2025 net Colorado tax (110% if 2025 federal AGI exceeded $150,000, or $75,000 MFS); the prior-year method requires a full 12-month 2025 Colorado return.

businessCosts.llcFormationFee: $50 Articles of Organization (online only), Colorado Secretary of State.
businessCosts.annualReportFee: $25 Periodic Report, filed every year ($50 late penalty).
